name: Godot
category: A7. Native applications and procedural tools
role: Godot headless and --write-movie runs scripted scenes to frames or video, in 2D and 3D
summary: Open-source game engine. Scenes and GDScript run from the command line, and --write-movie renders a scene at a fixed frame rate to PNG sequence or AVI with a fixed timestep, so frame N follows the game clock. Strength is interactive-style 2D and 3D scenes with physics and shaders as video. Needs a real renderer: --headless gives no pixels.
use_when: Game-like scenes with physics, tilemaps or shaders that should become video
Over Blender when the scene is already a Godot project
Fixed-timestep capture of an interactive prototype via --write-movie
2D sprite and particle scenes needing an engine scene tree
avoid_when: Offline-quality lighting or path tracing: Blender Cycles
Pure DOM or SVG motion: GSAP
Headless CI without a GPU or display: Blender Workbench or Three.js
notes: 2026-10-26: Movie Maker mode behaviour on Apple Silicon and with --headless was not tested; only the command-line documentation was consulted.

assessment.rationale: 4.7.2 stable released 2026-08-18; Homebrew cask tracks it. Command-line and movie-writing modes are documented. Renders need a graphics backend, so it is a native-application route, not a headless one.
